harness_contract.symbol_namespace: All IDs below are fixture-local symbols, not real event IDs, source identities, handles, grants or bearer tokens.
harness_contract.ingress: Adapters construct the existing frozen event envelope using synthetic connectors. This fixture object must never be admitted directly or used to widen production codecs.

admission_modes.meaning: A future adapter prepares checked, fully grounded admissions from the current prefix to test deterministic lifecycle mechanics. Owner identity controls test only their explicit authority path.

Run the pinned configured producer on current-prefix source records only. Compare its independent output against the oracle. Do not seed claims or identity results in this mode; report unresolved/unsupported outcomes and false merges.

harness_contract.oracle_isolation: Runner sends only released input records/control operations to the system under test. Future records, future controls, this oracle, provider draft and expected answers are inaccessible to retrieval, consolidation, tuning and prediction prompts.
harness_contract.historical_policy: Semantic reconstruction uses records/controls available at known_at. Current authorization, erasure and restore validity are evaluated at delivery_at and can refuse disclosure of an otherwise historical answer.
harness_contract.input_slice_rule: For a query, raw captures require Core accepted_at <= known_at; interpreted state additionally requires its own Core admitted_at/admission_seq <= the query boundary. Semantic controls require their own Core admission <= known_at. Source-observed or occurrence time cannot make later raw/semantic state known earlier. Current authorization/erasure/restore controls gate delivery at delivery_at without injecting later semantic content.
harness_contract.controls_are_trusted_calls: Owner controls are authenticated harness operations with explicit narrow authority. Identical text captured in a source is untrusted data and has no control authority.
harness_contract.grounding: Every expected support selection refers to one exact synthetic event version and full-text UTF-16 span. Production adapters must compute and verify the real admitted hash; fixture checksums must not substitute for product evidence.
harness_contract.currentness: Unknown domain facts may appear in a complete view. Missing required dependencies, history or required context may not be hidden behind current/unchanged/empty success.
harness_contract.purity: All people, sources, phrases and times are synthetic. No external accounts, private vaults or model calls are required to parse or validate this file.
harness_contract.source_restriction: Restricted S4 uses existing subject-scope denial, not a new sensitivity enum or per-principal source ACL. Each source capture carries only its source-local raw subject. g1 initially grants all four; g2 excludes scope_s4. Both retain private ceiling. Actor mentions do not add a second granted ingress subject; identity resolution never expands that source scope. Source-global consent is checked independently.
harness_contract.recorded_time: available_at is the trusted simulated release instant; sourceObservedAt/record_created_at/record_occurrence are source assertions. Only the Core clock may stamp accepted_at and admission recorded times. Controlled-mechanics schedule below uses simulated Core transactions. Real producer quality runs record actual accepted/admission times and never backdate them.
harness_contract.wire_projection: Future wire codecs use typed principal-namespace opaque references for objects, claims, events/versions and receipts, without raw internal IDs or source hashes. An absent/purged/revoked/denied/wrong-namespace well-formed object reference yields the same fixed not_found; new_view_required is exclusively a view/cursor outcome. Closed envelope/v2 omits source_policy.epoch, denied counts and other global metadata on every read; narrow legacy contracts refuse fixed unsupported before candidate discovery.
harness_contract.unknown_token: Token tests use a configured reserved principal partition; no token quota/expiry is extended. Complete fresh reads for an unreserved principal may return current with view.status not_issued and cannot be used as a token baseline.
harness_contract.snapshot_lifetime: Proposed snapshot/view repeatability lasts only while its cache token remains valid, with 900-second TTL and principal-local quota eviction. Restart/restore rotates the view runtime generation; durable authorization namespaces and supported random object-reference mappings are distinct.

principals.scope: Explicit scoped read and narrow correction relay; distinct from built-in OWNER. Owner-plane purge/restore is performed separately by the trusted isolated harness.
principals.future_view_cache_reservation: Explicit synthetic owner-plane reservation required before token comparison; no hidden-source-driven allocation.

records.content: Ada Vale reports: I read a definition of idempotency at 10:00 on 2 January 2025. Idempotency means repeating the same operation has the same effect as doing it once. Fixture marker: cobalt-teacup.
Ben Reed independently writes: In computing, idempotency means applying an operation repeatedly has the same effect as applying it once. Setting a flag to true is an example.
A. Vale asks: Should a copied account of the same retry count as independent evidence? The author and original question time are otherwise unknown.
Ben Reed writes: Idempotency is also the codename of our paper sculpture project. This project name does not refer to the computing concept.
Ada Vale reports: I read a definition of idempotency at 10:00 on 2 January 2025. Idempotency means repeating the same operation has the same effect as doing it once. Fixture marker: cobalt-teacup.
